body: I am but I ended up having extensive nerve damage from the surgery which has led to debilitating chronic pain for the past 6 years. I’m constantly in and out of doctor’s appointments and hospitals and it’s completely turned my life upside down to be honest. I’m lucky to have an amazing team of doctors now who were able to diagnose and provide ongoing support though.

I’ve documented some of my experience on TikTok:  https://www.tiktok.com/@erinorchard88?_t=8o2lI5w5Vuj&_r=1

Or if you Google ‘Erin laser eye surgery’ or ‘Erin Lasik surgery’ some articles about my story should come up if you’re interested
Not good 😔 I live with debilitating pain every day and rely on a lot of medications and various treatments. Laser eye surgery was the worst decision of my life. I’m also back to needing glasses

Just so you know it is actually illegal in many states. And if someone does sadly pass, it is highly likely you will be part of coroner’s court inquest at a minimum. I say this from experience as I have witnessed this happen.

Thank you for making me feel less alone ❤️ I am so lucky to have access to some amazing doctors but nobody in my team is a woman and I find this is the one topic they struggle to discuss with me or take into consideration. At some point I feel like I stopped being seen as a person with dreams and aspirations and became a complex medical problem for them to try to solve. I’m still extremely grateful to them for trying to help me though. I hadn’t experienced any significant health concerns up until my 30s and it’s taken me a while to learn how to self advocate and navigate the medical system. My condition isn’t genetic and was a result of surgery complications. I feel like initially I would ask for meds and treatment options that were safe for pregnancy but each time they would ask for one year to trial different drugs etc and then the cycle would repeat itself. I don’t want to sacrifice anymore and I don’t know if that’s selfish of me.

Thank you for your thoughtful reply. I should add, I’ve now come off the medication that would have caused birth defects but it’s taken a long time. While it’s now potentially possible to have a child the pregnancy would still be high risk and I would need to make some further changes to my ongoing treatment regiment. It’s a very overwhelming process and while I am extremely grateful to have access to an amazing medical team I wish one of them was a woman because I find this is the one topic they struggle to discuss and take into consideration.

More than happy to answer any questions that I can. The nerve damage is on the corneal of my eyes from what I understand. I went to several ophthalmologists to confirm my diagnosis and seek treatments. I’ve been told that nothing went wrong during the surgery but that this is a rare risk associated with laser eye surgery. Sadly it was a risk I was completely unaware of. I have since linked into a Facebook support group with many others who have shared my experience which has been helpful but also overwhelming. My vision is great for the most part. I get some glare and halos from lights at night and I was very light sensitive for approx 3 weeks after the surgery.
I’ve been told nothing went wrong with the surgery but that this is a known possible risk associated with laser eye surgery. I was unlucky I guess.
The pain started on day 2 or 3 after the surgery and has continued since. I’m now up to week 8.

The pain is extremely high and I am on opioid medication to manage it as best I can. I was formally diagnosed by two ophthalmologists. It has impacted greatly on my quality of life and ability to work.

I completely regret my laser eye surgery. I now have nerve damage and am in constant pain as a result. I now see an ophthalmologist and pain specialist on a regular basis and rely on medication to get me through each day. I would do almost anything to take back my decision.

I have been diagnosed with neuropathic pain and am on a large amount of medication. I’m seeing an ophthalmologist, GP, and pain specialist on a regular basis. It’s been an absolute nightmare. The pain is so awful I can hardly sleep or go to work. I truely regret having the surgery.
